gold: Rent reporting lets renters build a credit score without taking on debt.
There are 22 million Gen Z renters in the US and about 70% have no credit history that qualifies them for a prime card.
All three bureaus began accepting rent tradelines from third-party reporters in 2024, enabling a consumer product now.
Reporting rent raises a thin-file user's score by an average of 40 points within six months, per Quill's cohort data.
The $4 a month premium tier is bought by 30% of active users.
Quill has 18,000 monthly active users growing 25% month over month with zero paid acquisition.
60% of users who connect a bank account are still active after 90 days.
The founders built the rent-payment product at a property-management software company processing $2B a year in rent.
The product requires minimal user effort: connect a bank account and Quill identifies and reports the rent payment monthly.
forbidden: The bureaus could change their reporting rules (risk).
Large banks could bundle rent reporting for free (risk).
Premium attach rate may fall as the base broadens (risk).
The ask: $2.5M seed at $15M post, taking $1M.
